settings.description: Every line of CourseLit is public on GitHub. Self-hosted CourseLit has every feature with no licence key, and the cloud is there if you would rather not run servers.

settings.title: Why open source matters here
settings.description: Your school should not depend on one company staying in business.

items.title: No lock-in
items.description: The code is public, so you can host it, change it or fork it. Your data stays in a PostgreSQL database you control.

items.title: Every feature, no licence key
items.description: Set BILLING_MODE to oss and every school on your deployment gets every plan feature, including SCORM and single sign-on.

items.title: Built in the open
items.description: Read the code, report issues and send changes on GitHub, or ask questions in the community on Discord.

settings.title: What a self-hosted deployment is made of
settings.body:
Each release publishes three container images:

- `codelit/courselit-api`: the REST API, the MCP server and all business logic. The same image also runs the background worker.
- `codelit/courselit-admin`: the dashboard where you manage your school.
- `codelit/courselit-storefront`: the public websites your learners use.

The only data store is **PostgreSQL**. You also bring an external **media storage** service and an **email** service, either SMTP or a team key. One deployment can serve many schools.

[Deploy the services](/docs/self-hosting/deploy)

settings.title: What to expect today
settings.body:
CourseLit 1.0 is in pre-release, and self-hosting is for experienced operators. There is **no one-command installer** and **no production Compose file**, so you assemble the services yourself. Details can change between pre-releases, and moving between them may need a fresh database.

If you only want to teach and sell, the cloud is the easier path.

[Read the self-hosting overview](/docs/self-hosting)

items.question: What licence is CourseLit under?
items.answer: AGPL-3.0. The code is public on GitHub and has been since 2019.

items.question: Is there a paid edition of self-hosted CourseLit?
items.answer: No. Self-hosted CourseLit has every feature and needs no licence key. You pay only for the servers and services you run.

items.question: Can I run more than one school?
items.answer: Yes. One deployment serves many schools. Each gets a subdomain of your platform domain and can attach a custom domain.

items.question: Which version should I deploy?
items.answer: Pin an explicit version tag and use the same one for all three images. Pre-releases never move the latest tag, which still points at the older 0.x line.

items.question: Where do I get help?
items.answer: Ask in the community on Discord, and report bugs or send changes on GitHub.
